gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: Wrap up warm, or you'll ___ a cold.
gaps.explanation: catch a cold is the fixed collocation for becoming ill with one.

gaps.sentence: Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.

gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.

gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a visit to the museum while we were in Vienna.
gaps.explanation: pay a visit to somebody/something means to go and see them briefly.
